pages.text:
1. One World, Seven Lands
2. Africa: Our Own Home
3. Asia: The Largest of All
4. Europe: Small but Crowded
5. The Americas: North and South
6. Australia and Antarctica
7. One Human Family

continent: one of the Earth's seven great land regions
ocean: one of the vast seas that cover most of the Earth
desert: a very dry land where little rain falls
rainforest: a thick, wet forest full of life
equator: the imaginary line round the middle of the Earth
population: the number of people living in a place

If you could rise high enough to see the whole Earth at once, you would see it is mostly blue, wrapped in vast oceans. Poking up out of that blue are the great pieces of land where nearly all living things dwell. We divide these lands into seven huge regions, and we call each one a continent.

image.note: The whole Earth from space, oceans blue, the seven continents visible; a wide, beautiful view

pages.text: The seven continents are Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Australia and Antarctica. Each is different from the others in its land, its weather, its animals and its people. Yet all are joined by the same seas and the same sky. Let us travel round them, and begin, of course, at home.

image.note: A flat world map with the seven continents each in a different warm colour, labelled

pages.text: Africa is our continent, the second largest in the world, and one of the most varied. In its north lies the Sahara, the greatest hot desert on Earth, a sea of sand larger than many whole continents. Yet Africa also holds thick green rainforests, vast grassy plains, and snow on its highest mountains near the equator.

image.note: A montage of Africa: golden Sahara dunes, green rainforest, grassy savanna with acacia trees

pages.text: Africa is the place where the very first humans lived, which makes it, in a way, the original home of everyone on Earth. Today it holds over fifty countries and more than a billion people, speaking well over a thousand languages. Nigeria, your own country, is the most populated of them all. Africa is old, huge, and gloriously full of life.

image.note: A lively African street scene, many peoples, colourful clothes, busy market; Nigeria highlighted on a small map

pages.text: Across a narrow join to the north-east of Africa lies Asia, by far the largest continent, and the most crowded. More people live in Asia than on all the other continents put together. It stretches from hot tropical islands to the frozen north, and holds the highest mountains on Earth, the mighty Himalayas.

image.note: The Himalayas towering with snow; a busy Asian city below; the sheer scale of Asia

pages.text: Asia gave the world some of its oldest cities and greatest ideas. Writing, farming and many faiths began there. Two countries, China and India, each hold well over a billion people. From the deserts of Arabia to the rice fields of the far east, Asia is a continent of astonishing size and variety.

image.note: A split image: Arabian desert with camels; green terraced rice fields in the far east

pages.text: To the west of Asia, joined onto it, lies Europe. It is one of the smallest continents, yet it is packed with many countries crowded close together. For a few centuries, as you may have read, European countries built empires that stretched across much of the world, including our own.

image.note: A map of Europe crowded with small countries; historic cities with old stone buildings

pages.text: Europe has cold, snowy winters in much of it, quite unlike the warmth of home. Its long history has left it full of ancient castles, grand old cities and famous museums, some of which, it must be said, hold treasures taken from other lands, including African art still waiting to come home.

image.note: A grand European museum; among its cases, a Benin bronze; a quiet, honest note

pages.text: Far across the ocean to the west lie two joined continents, North America and South America. Long before ships arrived from Europe, great civilisations flourished there, building cities and pyramids of their own. Their peoples had lived there for thousands of years, with rich cultures all their own.

image.note: An ancient American pyramid in a jungle; indigenous people in fine dress; dignified, pre-arrival

pages.text: North America today holds wealthy, powerful countries and huge modern cities. South America holds the mighty Amazon, the largest rainforest on Earth, a green world so vast it makes its own weather and breathes out much of the air we share. From frozen north to steaming jungle, the Americas hold nearly every kind of land.

image.note: Split image: a North American city skyline; the endless green Amazon rainforest and its river

pages.text: Far to the south lies Australia, the smallest continent, a single great country surrounded by sea. It is famous for strange animals found nowhere else, that hop, or carry their babies in pouches. Its first peoples have lived there for tens of thousands of years, among the oldest cultures on the whole planet.

image.note: The Australian outback, red earth, a kangaroo; Aboriginal rock art on a cliff; unique

pages.text: Last comes Antarctica, at the very bottom of the world, the coldest, windiest, emptiest continent of all. It is buried under ice deeper than the tallest towers, and no people live there permanently, only scientists who visit to study it. It is a frozen, silent land, kept wild and shared by all nations.

image.note: The white Antarctic ice sheet, penguins, a small research base; vast, empty, cold

pages.text: Seven continents, then, each a world of its own. And yet, look closer and something binds them all. On every one of them, wherever the land will allow it, you find people, living, working, raising children, telling stories. We are spread across the whole Earth, but we are one single family, sharing one small planet.

image.note: Children of many lands, one from each continent, standing together holding a globe; unity

pages.text: When you find your own home on a map, remember this. You are one child, in one city, in one country, on one continent, on one blue world spinning in space. The whole vast Earth, all seven of its great lands, is your home too, and its story is now partly yours to write. Go and see as much of it as you can.

image.note: A child pointing to Nigeria on a globe, then looking up and outward; hopeful, closing
